text:
raj: Seeing a spike of 502s from eu-west-edge for the inference svc after several spot GPU preemptions. LB is still routing to IPs that should be gone. Anyone seen this pattern before?

matt: which svc / LB type? headless or ClusterIP -> NodePort?

raj: Not headless. Service is ClusterIP backed by EndpointSlices that we use as LB targets on the edge. Problem looks like stale endpoints remaining in the slices after nodes were preempted.

lina: ugh. Are kube-proxy/ipvs rules not being cleaned up on the drained nodes?

raj: I SSH'd into one of the old nodes (eu-edge-spot-42) before it was terminated. kube-proxy was still around and there were conntrack entries referencing the pod IPs. Pasted clipped outputs below.

raj: ```bash
$ kubectl get endpointslice -n inference -o yaml | sed -n '1,120p'
apiVersion: discovery.k8s.io/v1
items:
- metadata:
    name: inference-svc-6f7b2
  endpoints:
  - addresses:
    - 10.240.3.62
    conditions:
      ready: false
    nodeName: eu-edge-spot-42
  - addresses:
    - 10.240.4.11
    conditions:
      ready: true
    nodeName: eu-edge-12
... (trimmed)
```

raj: And conntrack on the node showed entries to 10.240.3.62:

raj: ```bash
# conntrack -L | grep 10.240.3.62
tcp      6 431999 ESTABLISHED src=34.89.12.1 dst=10.240.3.62 sport=443 dport=32456 packets=12 bytes=1204 src=10.240.3.62 dst=34.89.12.1 sport=32456 dport=443 packets=10 bytes=1020
```

matt: so path: autoscaler preempts node -> pods scheduled elsewhere -> endpointslice should update -> LB keeps hitting old IPs because ipvs/iptables or conntrack still have state on the egress path?

lina: could be two things: 1) endpointslice controller didn't remove the endpoint quickly because the node status flapped, or 2) kube-proxy on the node kept iptables/ipvs state that the edge LB used for endpoint selection. Which LB do we use at the edge (external NLB or metal LB)?

raj: external NLB with nodePort targets. NodePort->kube-proxy->pod, so stale ipvs rules/conntrack can make traffic land on dead pods.

matt: quick debug steps: force endpointslice resync, check controller-manager logs for endpoint reconciler errors, and rotate kube-proxy on affected nodes to clear ipvs state.

lina: agreed. Workaround that helped last time: restart kube-proxy on the drained node (or cordon + drain and let it terminate) then run `kubectl delete endpointslice inference-svc-6f7b2 -n inference` to force rebuild. Not ideal permanent fix.

raj: I restarted kube-proxy on the node that was still up and the 502s subsided after the controller reconciled (~15s). We should add a reconcile hook when nodes go NotReady/Terminated in the autoscaler path.

matt: open a short postmortem and a follow-up to add a post-drain API call in the autoscaler to trigger endpointslice reconcile (or mark Node as terminating earlier so controller removes endpoints faster). Also consider adding a kube-proxy restart toleration to the node termination handler.

lina: I'll create a GH issue for autoscaler -> endpointslice reconciliation and add a short runbook: on 502 spike, check_endpointslice.sh, restart kube-proxy, force delete slice.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INF-2026-34 - eu-west-edge: LB 502s due to stale endpoints / kube-proxy conntrack. Assigned: eng-infra oncall.

raj: tagging @matt and @lina for the follow-ups. I'll attach node logs and controller-manager excerpts to the GH issue. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
